title: Kelewele with Calabash Nutmeg
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: A tablespoon of black peppercorns and ten cloves alongside calabash nutmeg and aniseed — and her own flag is that the spices will not stick.
longDesc: The most aggressively spiced documented kelewele: two large ripened plantains against one calabash nutmeg or six allspice pods, ten cloves, a tablespoon of black peppercorns, a teaspoon of aniseed, thirty grams of ginger, an onion and a habanero or five dried red chillies. Black peppercorns in kelewele appear in no other source. Her honest note is the problem the dish actually has — difficulty getting the spices to stick to the ripened plantain when it fries — and she says the video covers it. The method is video-only, so the steps here are reconstructed.
ingredients: 1 habanero chilli, or 5 dried red chillies
steps: // The published method for this recipe is video-only. No written steps exist in the source.
Grind the aniseed, calabash nutmeg, cloves and black peppercorns.
Blend the onion, ginger and chilli with a little water.
Combine the ground spices with the blended aromatics and salt.
Cube the plantains and coat them with the spice mixture.
Rest briefly so the coating adheres.
Fry in hot oil in batches until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
// The order above is inferred from the other documented kelewele, not from this source.
chefTips: Her own flag is the real problem with kelewele and worth knowing before you start: it is difficult to get the spices to stick to ripened plantain when it fries. Resting the coated cubes and keeping the marinade thick rather than watery both help.
A tablespoon of black peppercorns is unique to this version among all documented kelewele. It gives a sharper, less sweet result.
Calabash nutmeg — ehuru — is not true nutmeg and tastes nothing like it. Six allspice pods is her stated alternative, and that is a real substitution rather than an equivalent.
Ten cloves for two plantains is a very high ratio. If that sounds like a lot, it is, and it is printed as such.
Grind the whole spices yourself. Pre-ground loses the volatile oils that make the difference here.
Two plantains makes this the smallest documented batch, which suits the heavy spicing — scale the plantain up and the spices will overwhelm.
The method is reconstructed from the other documented kelewele. Nothing in the step order is this author's.
commonMistakes: Treating the reconstructed step order as the author's own.
Using true nutmeg in place of calabash nutmeg.
A watery marinade, which will not cling.
Scaling the plantain up without scaling the spices.
Frying before the coating has had a moment to adhere.
sources: Quantities from 'KELEWELE: The Traditional Ghanaian Spiced Plantain Snack', byline as printed 'Fafa Gilbert', 25 February 2021, on her site where she styles herself 'The Flavour & Claypot Chef'. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS). Fafa Gilbert is Ewe, from the Volta Region, per her own site — the basis for the community attribution.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 2 large ripened Plantain; 1 medium sized Onion; 1 teaspoon of Aniseed; 1 Calabash Nutmeg or 6 Allspice pods; 10 cloves; 1 tablespoon of Black Peppercorns; 1 Habanero Chilli or 5 dried Red Chillies; 30g of fresh Ginger; Salt to taste. NOTE that no oil quantity is given.

METHOD GAP, stated plainly: NO WRITTEN METHOD, NO FRYING TEMPERATURE and NO DONENESS CUE exist in the source — the instructions are video-only. The steps in this entry are explicitly marked as reconstructed from GHA049, and the step list carries a header saying so.

HER FLAGGED DIFFICULTY, verbatim: 'difficulty in getting the spices to stick to the ripened Plantain when fried'. She notes the video addresses it. That is an honest statement of the dish's actual failure mode and it is the most useful thing on the page.
BLACK PEPPERCORNS are unique to this version among the five documented kelewele spice systems. So is the allspice-pod alternative to calabash nutmeg.

WHY IT IS PUBLISHED DESPITE THE METHOD GAP: the spice system is documented nowhere else, every spice carries a quantity, and the author's flagged difficulty is genuinely instructive. The entry is published for the ingredient list with its method honestly labelled as inferred.
ON CALABASH NUTMEG: Monodora myristica, also ehuru or African nutmeg, botanically unrelated to true nutmeg.
For the full five-source comparison of kelewele spice systems and frying temperatures, and the Ghanaian Times etymology and origin claim, see the sources at GHA049.
healthBenefits: Ripe plantain supplies potassium, vitamin A and vitamin B6.
Cloves are among the highest-antioxidant spices measured.
Calabash nutmeg and aniseed both carry documented aromatic compounds.
culturalNote: Spicing kelewele this heavily — peppercorns, ten cloves, calabash nutmeg — pushes it toward the aromatic end of Ghanaian cooking that the Volta Region favours generally, the same instinct that puts selim pods and dawadawa into palmnut soup. The street version in Accra is far plainer.
